title: A Cooking Class
story:
On Thursday evening, Samir joined a cooking class in a small room above the library. He tied an apron and washed his hands at the long sink. The teacher, Noor, wrote a simple recipe on the board. They were going to make tomato pasta for two people. Samir copied the steps into his notebook so he would not forget the order.

First, Noor showed them how to chop an onion into small pieces. Samir's pieces were uneven, but he kept the knife slow and safe. Next he measured olive oil in a spoon and warmed it in a pan. When the onion turned soft, he added chopped tomatoes and a pinch of salt. Noor told the class to let the sauce simmer, not boil hard. The bubbles stayed small, and the smell grew sweet.

While the sauce cooked, Samir boiled pasta in a deep pot. He stirred it once so it would not stick. Noor walked around and tasted a few sauces. She said Samir needed a little more salt, then a few leaves of basil. He added them and tasted again. At the end, the students ate at the counter and compared their plates. Noor gave each person a card with the same recipe and space for notes. Samir wrote "simmer slowly" and "taste before you serve". He left the class with the card in his bag and a plan to cook the dish for his flatmate on Saturday.
